edges.description: PYCR1 performs the final reduction of pyrroline-5-carboxylate to proline, so its loss is expected to reduce de novo proline synthesis.
Fibroblasts from affected individuals show altered mitochondria. Whether this follows from proline shortage, altered NAD(P)H redox balance, or another PYCR1 function is unresolved.

edges.description: PYCR1 loss is associated with hypotonia, psychomotor delay and variable intellectual disability; the neural mechanism is unknown, and severity tracks the location of the variant.
Prenatal growth restriction is a hallmark of PYCR1 deficiency; the mechanism is unknown.
Postnatal growth deficiency accompanies PYCR1 deficiency; the mechanism is unknown.
Strabismus occurs in about a third of evaluated patients; the mechanism is unknown.
Lens opacity occurs in a minority of patients; the mechanism is unknown.
Glaucoma has been reported in individual patients; the mechanism is unknown.
Reduced bone mineralization occurs in PYCR1 deficiency; the bone mechanism is unknown.
Wormian bones are reported in PYCR1 deficiency; the mechanism is unknown.
An open or large fontanel is reported in PYCR1 deficiency; the mechanism is unknown.
Adducted thumbs are reported in PYCR1 deficiency; the mechanism is unknown.
Aortic root dilatation was reported in one de Barsy patient; the mechanism is unknown.
Elastin is a proline-rich protein abundant in the most affected tissues, so reduced local proline supply is the proposed link to the connective-tissue phenotype. This remains a hypothesis.
Mitochondrially compromised PYCR1-deficient cells are hypersensitive to oxidative stress and undergo more apoptosis.
edges.source: Mitochondrial Morphology and Membrane Potential Defect

edges.description: Loss of skin cells by apoptosis is the proposed route to cutaneous hypoplasia; in pycr1 knockdown frog and fish embryos epidermal hypoplasia accompanies a large rise in apoptosis.
Elastic-fibre and collagen changes in the dermis are the tissue substrate of lax skin.
Dermal and subcutaneous connective-tissue loss presents as thin skin.
Lax dermis wrinkles, most visibly on the dorsum of the hands and feet.
Thin skin with little subcutaneous fat leaves superficial veins visible.
Loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue is part of the progeroid tissue phenotype.
The skin and fat changes produce the progeroid appearance.
Facial lipoatrophy and thin skin contribute to the triangular progeroid face.
Joint laxity accompanies the connective-tissue phenotype; the periarticular mechanism is not studied.
Hip dislocation is attributed to connective-tissue laxity; the mechanism is not studied.
Hernias are attributed to connective-tissue weakness of the abdominal wall; the mechanism is not studied in PYCR1 disease.
Flat feet are attributed to ligamentous laxity; the mechanism is not studied in PYCR1 disease.
Blue sclerae are taken to reflect thin scleral connective tissue; scleral histology has not been reported in PYCR1 disease.
A corneal button from a PYCR1 patient showed loss of the stromal lamellar architecture, a connective-tissue defect of the cornea.
Reproduces increased apoptosis and reduced antioxidant capacity in vivo.
edges.limitations: Fish skin, lifespan and paralogue complement differ from human; the ageing and behavioural phenotypes have no direct human counterpart in the congenital disorder.

nodes.description: Skin of affected individuals shows smaller and fragmented elastic fibres and irregular collagen fibrils, with loss of subcutaneous fat.
